ST. JOHN - Chapter 1 < Previous Chapter ----- Next Chapter >
John i.

Notes & Commentary:

Ver. 1. In the beginning was the word:[1] or rather, the word was in the beginning. The eternal word, the increated[uncreated?] wisdom, the second Person of the blessed Trinity, as he is here called (ver. 14.) of the same nature with the Father and Holy Ghost. --- Philo Judæus, in the apostolic age, uses the word Logos, p. 823, to personify the wisdom and the power of God. (Haydock)

Ver. 2. The same was in the beginning with God. In the text is only, "this was in the beginning;" but the sense and construction certainly is, this word was in the beginning. (Witham)

Ver. 8-9. He; that is John the Baptist, was not the true light: but the word was the true light. (Witham)

Ver. 14. And the word was made flesh. This word, or Son of God, who was in the beginning, from all eternity, was made flesh, i.e. became man. --- As of the only begotten of the Father.[3] St. Chrysostom and others take notice that the word as, no ways diminisheth the signification. (Witham)

____________________

[1] Ver. 1. Et Deus erat Verbum, kai theos en o logos. Logos was a word very proper to give all that should believe a right notion of the Messias. See Walton, prolog. xii.

[3] Ver. 14. Gloriam quasi Unigeniti, os monogenous. St. Chrysostom says, the word quasi, os, does no ways here diminish, but even confirms and increases the signification.

[5] A note the transcriber attached to no verse.
Bible Text & Cross-references:

The divinity and incarnation of Christ. John bears witness of him. He begins to call his disciples.

1 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
2 The same was in the beginning with God.
3 All things were made by him: and without him was made nothing that was made.
6 *There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.
8 He was not the light, but was to bear witness of the light.
9 *That was the true light, which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world.
14 *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: and we saw his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.
15 John beareth witness of him: and crieth out, saying: This was he of whom I spoke, He that shall come after me, is preferred before me, because he was before me.

6: Matthew iii. 1.; Mark i. 4.
9: John iii. 19.
14: Matthew i. 16.; Luke ii. 7.
